decisions.costs: Reading a parent with its children needs a second query (or $lookup) instead of one document fetch.
decisions.gains: posts grows without bound (temporal column, no natural cap); keeping it separate avoids the 16 MB document ceiling and whole-document rewrites on every append.
decisions.mitigations: If recent-children reads matter, add a capped 'recent' array on the parent and treat it as a cache, not the system of record.
decisions.subject: edge:authors->posts

decisions.costs: Renaming a categories value means a fan-out update across every posts document that carries it.
decisions.gains: categories is a small, read-only lookup: duplicating (name) into posts documents removes the join from hot reads while the code field remains the join key for repairs.
decisions.mitigations: Lookups like this rarely change; when they do, batch-repair by the join key. The lookup collection can be dropped: nothing in the workload reads it alone.
decisions.subject: edge:categories->posts

decisions.costs: Recursive traversal (whole subtrees) needs recursive CTEs in SQL and $graphLookup in MongoDB — neither is free.
decisions.gains: Adjacency lists are index-friendly, handle arbitrary depth, and match how comment threads and org charts are actually queried.
decisions.mitigations: If whole-subtree reads dominate, maintain a materialized path field (path '/a/b/c') as a derived, repairable index.

decisions.costs: Removing a tags from the vocabulary means updating every host document that carries it; the array index is multikey.
decisions.gains: tags is a bounded vocabulary: an array of ids + name on each posts document answers the co-accessed reads in one fetch, one-way (no dual arrays to keep consistent).
decisions.mitigations: Vocabulary changes are rare; repair by scanning the array field when they happen.
